key_insight: The paper argues that true visual understanding is not a one-shot snapshot process, but a loop of observing, hypothesizing, and re-checking. It introduces ActiveVision to measure whether multimodal LLMs actually perform this kind of active observation.
problem_solved: Current vision-language benchmarks mainly test final answers, not whether models actively direct attention or gaze based on intermediate hypotheses. This paper addresses the lack of an empirical way to evaluate active observation in multimodal large language models.
method: Introduces ActiveVision, a benchmark designed to make active observation measurable for MLLMs.
Frames evaluation around whether models revise or redirect their visual focus in response to intermediate reasoning.
Compares model behavior against the idea of human-like closed-loop vision rather than static image understanding.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a new way to test whether multimodal systems truly inspect images intelligently instead of relying on superficial pattern matching. It can guide the design of models that reason more like humans in visually complex tasks.
visual_elements: Closed-loop vision diagram showing gaze -> hypothesis -> re-gaze -> answer
